title: Europe's free satellite service just made it easier to track wildfires
gist: On August 4 the Copernicus Browser added a default 'wildfires' visualization layer for Sentinel-2 imagery, built from a near-decade-old JavaScript band-combination script by remote sensing expert Pierre Markuse and pushed into the product by ESA Sentinel-2 mission scientist Simon Proud. The change makes 10-meter multispectral fire monitoring available to anyone for free, a resolution advantage over NASA's faster-updating but 250-meter FIRMS tool.

insights.claim: The Copernicus Browser added a straightforward 'wildfires' visualization layer for Sentinel-2 imagery that went live on August 4, adding to the 10 default visualization layers it previously offered.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A dated, concrete capability release — the point at which expert-only tooling became one-click accessible for fire monitoring.

insights.claim: The wildfire layer renders active fires in white or yellow, burning vegetation in red, and burned landscapes in dark brown or black, so interpretation requires no remote sensing expertise.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Legibility to non-specialists is what converts an imagery archive into an operational public tool for journalists and responders.

insights.claim: The visualization comes from a JavaScript script by remote sensing expert Pierre Markuse that combines the red visible band, the narrow near-infrared band to separate healthy from burned vegetation, and the short-wave infrared 2 band to reveal soil moisture and burned landscape.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The specific three-band recipe is the reusable technical content — it can be applied to any multispectral sensor, not just Sentinel-2.

insights.claim: Users could already apply the same script manually by copying and pasting it into the Copernicus Browser custom visualization option, so the update removed a friction barrier rather than adding new capability.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Distribution, not technology, was the binding constraint — a reminder that default settings determine real-world adoption of open data.
insights.locator: 'Users could previously add this script manually'

insights.claim: Simon Proud, the European Space Agency's mission scientist for Sentinel-2, pushed to get the script integrated as a default option and announced the integration in a Discord channel on a server run by the investigative journalism group Bellingcat.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: An ESA product change announced first to an OSINT community shows where the demand for this tooling actually originates.
insights.locator: 'But Simon Proud, mission scientist for Sentinel-2'

insights.claim: The three satellites of the Sentinel-2 mission provide multi-spectral imaging at resolutions as granular as 10 meters in visible light and near-infrared bands, which is why they have proven especially useful for wildfire monitoring.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: 10-meter multispectral is the free-tier resolution ceiling — the benchmark any commercial imagery vendor must beat to justify a price.

insights.claim: NASA's FIRMS tool offers a free global map of satellite-detected fires updated within several hours, but only at coarser resolutions down to 250 meters.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: FIRMS wins on latency, Sentinel-2 on detail — the two are complements, and users needing both must stitch them together.
insights.locator: 'There are other existing and emerging satellite constellations'

insights.claim: Sentinel-2 imagery updates only every few days versus FIRMS' several-hour refresh, making it a post-hoc assessment tool rather than a real-time detection system.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The revisit gap defines the unfilled market slot: high-resolution plus high-cadence fire imagery is what commercial constellations can still sell.

insights.claim: Sentinel-2 is arguably the best free and publicly available tool for higher-resolution satellite imagery of everything from wildfires to war zones, extending its relevance well beyond disaster monitoring.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Dual-use framing explains why an OSINT community drove the feature — the same layer serves conflict verification, not just fire response.
insights.quote: That makes it arguably the best free and publicly available tool for delivering higher-resolution satellite imagery of everything from wildfires to war zones.

insights.claim: Climate change is exacerbating traditional wildfire seasons, with much of Washington and Oregon experiencing fires and smoke, Canada's season on track to be one of its worst, and firefighters battling blazes in France and Spain.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Simultaneous severe seasons across North America and Europe sustain structural demand for fire monitoring and remote sensing capacity.
insights.locator: 'Unfortunately, there is no shortage of wildfires'

insights.claim: Hundreds of thousands of people have evacuated in France and Spain during a record-breaking wildfire season.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Mass evacuations in Western Europe put fiscal and insurance pressure behind investment in EU Earth observation infrastructure.
insights.locator: 'Unfortunately, there is no shortage of wildfires'
